places.name: St. Mary's Islands
places.summary: Four small islands off Malpe, known for columnar basalt formations and shell beaches.
places.description: A protected island group off the Malpe coast where columnar basalt meets the Arabian Sea. Ferry access is seasonal and weather-dependent, so check current local guidance before travelling.
places.image_alt: Columnar basalt formations on St. Mary's Islands
places.historical_background: The island's formation belongs to geological time rather than documented human history. Karnataka Tourism describes the basalt columns as the result of sub-aerial sub-volcanic activity.
places.cultural_significance: The islands are a distinctive natural landmark reached from Malpe and form part of Udupi's coastal identity.
places.geographical_importance: The group lies off Malpe in Udupi district. Its columnar basalt and shell shore are the principal features highlighted by Karnataka Tourism.

places.name: Udupi Sri Krishna Matha
places.summary: A 13th-century temple and monastic centre in the heart of Udupi.
places.description: The Sri Krishna Matha is a major pilgrimage and learning centre in Udupi. Karnataka Tourism identifies its 13th-century foundation with Madhvacharya and describes the surrounding Ashta Mathas and Paryaya tradition.
places.image_alt: Entrance of Udupi Sri Krishna Matha
places.historical_background: Karnataka Tourism dates the foundation to the 13th century and attributes it to Madhvacharya. Stories such as the origin of Kanakana Kindi are presented as temple legend, not independently verified chronology.
places.cultural_significance: The temple's worship, the Ashta Mathas and the Paryaya succession are important parts of Udupi's religious and public life.
places.geographical_importance: The Matha is located in Udupi town, inland from the Arabian Sea and within reach of the Malpe coast.
places.architectural_details: The complex has developed over time around the shrine, mathas, courtyards and the Kanakana Kindi viewing window. Architectural details should be understood as a layered ensemble rather than assigned to one construction period.

places.name: Malpe Beach & Harbour
places.summary: A working coastal harbour and beach that serves as the departure point for St. Mary's Islands.
places.description: Malpe brings together a beach, fishing harbour and passenger boat connections to St. Mary's Islands. Boat operations depend on sea and weather conditions; visitors should confirm current service information locally.
places.image_alt: Malpe Beach on the Udupi coast
places.historical_background: Malpe's place in this guide is its continuing coastal and harbour role. The supplied district material does not establish a single founding date for the settlement.
places.cultural_significance: Fishing and maritime work remain part of the coast's living identity. The harbour is also a gateway for visitors travelling to the nearby islands.
places.geographical_importance: Malpe lies on the Udupi coast, a short road journey from Udupi town, with the island group offshore.
important_attractions: Boat departure point for St. Mary's Islands

places.name: Kadri Manjunatha Temple & Hills
places.summary: A historic temple complex on the Kadri hillside in Mangaluru.
places.description: Kadri Manjunatha Temple is a prominent heritage and worship site on the eastern side of Mangaluru. The temple, hillside setting and water features make it a distinctive stop within the city.
places.historical_background: The existing district record associates the complex with early medieval heritage and a bronze Lokeshwara image. Exact building phases require site-specific archaeological references and are not assigned a single date here.
places.cultural_significance: The temple remains an active place of worship and part of Mangaluru's layered religious heritage.
places.geographical_importance: The complex occupies a hill setting within Mangaluru, where the coastal plain begins to rise toward the Western Ghats.
places.architectural_details: The site includes a temple complex and traditional water features. Its surviving forms reflect multiple periods; this guide avoids attributing every structure to one style or date.

places.name: St. Aloysius Chapel
places.summary: A landmark chapel on Lighthouse Hill in central Mangaluru.
places.description: St. Aloysius Chapel is noted for its richly painted interior and its place within the St. Aloysius campus on Lighthouse Hill. The site offers a distinct example of Mangaluru's religious and educational history.
places.image_alt: Interior of St. Aloysius Chapel in Mangaluru
places.historical_background: The existing district material describes the chapel as a 19th-century building and associates its paintings with Jesuit artist Antonio Moscheni. Visitors should check the institution's current access guidance.
places.cultural_significance: The chapel is a landmark of Mangaluru's Christian heritage and an active part of an educational campus.
places.geographical_importance: The chapel stands on Lighthouse Hill in Mangaluru, overlooking the coastal city.
places.architectural_details: Its painted interior is the defining feature noted in the district record. The illustration on this page is original artwork, not a photograph of the chapel.

places.name: Panambur Beach
places.summary: A public beach on the Arabian Sea near Mangaluru's port area.
places.description: Panambur is a broad urban beach on Mangaluru's northern shoreline. It is an accessible place to experience the open coast; swimming and other activities should follow local safety notices and lifeguard guidance.
places.image_alt: Panambur Beach on Mangaluru's northern shoreline
places.historical_background: This page focuses on Panambur as a present-day coastal public space. The available source material does not identify a specific historical founding event.
places.cultural_significance: The beach is part of Mangaluru's everyday relationship with the Arabian Sea and its public waterfront.
places.geographical_importance: Panambur lies north of Mangaluru city near the New Mangalore Port area.

places.name: Gokarna & Mahabaleshwara Temple
places.summary: A pilgrimage town on the Uttara Kannada coast, known for its temple and nearby beaches.
places.description: Gokarna brings together a major Shiva pilgrimage centre and a distinctive coastal landscape. The town's beaches and temple precincts are living places; visitors should respect local customs and access rules.
places.historical_background: Gokarna's religious history is carried through temple traditions and pilgrimage. Traditional accounts are presented as traditions rather than verified dates for the surviving buildings.
places.cultural_significance: The Mahabaleshwara Temple is an important pilgrimage site, while the town's coastal setting supports a mix of religious and visitor activity.
places.geographical_importance: Gokarna sits between the Arabian Sea and the forested Western Ghats of Uttara Kannada.
places.architectural_details: The temple precinct is a living sacred site. Building dates and architectural phases should be verified with temple and archaeological records before assigning specific periods.

places.name: Murudeshwar Temple & Sea-facing Statue
places.summary: A contemporary temple landmark on the coast at Bhatkal taluk.
places.description: Murudeshwar's temple complex occupies a headland beside the Arabian Sea. Its prominent gopura and large Shiva statue shape the present-day coastal skyline.
places.image_alt: Murudeshwar Temple and the sea-facing Shiva statue
places.historical_background: The complex is presented here as a contemporary landmark. No construction date is assigned without a cited project or institutional record.
places.cultural_significance: The site is an active pilgrimage destination and a widely recognised landmark on the Uttara Kannada coast.
places.geographical_importance: The temple stands on a coastal headland at Murudeshwar, with the sea visible on multiple sides.
places.architectural_details: The tall gopura and monumental statue are prominent contemporary features of the complex.

places.name: Mirjan Fort
places.summary: A laterite fort near Kumta, set among the waterways and greenery of the coast.
places.description: Mirjan Fort is a historic site near Kumta. The Uttara Kannada district portal specifically notes its use of locally available red laterite stone and its location about 12 km from Kumta.
places.image_alt: Laterite walls and grounds of Mirjan Fort
places.historical_background: Mirjan is associated in regional accounts with the coastal kingdom of Gersoppa and Queen Chennabhairadevi. The district portal does not establish a precise construction date, so this guide does not state one as settled fact.
places.cultural_significance: The fort is a reminder of the coast's layered political and trading histories and remains a visible landmark in the Kumta area.
places.geographical_importance: The fort is near Mirjan village, approximately 12 km from Kumta according to the Uttara Kannada district portal.
places.architectural_details: The official district description identifies locally available red laterite as a construction material. The fort's walls and defensive layout are best read on site.

places.name: Yana Rock Formations
places.summary: Distinctive dark rock outcrops in the forested Western Ghats.
places.description: Yana is known for dramatic rock outcrops and a forest approach in Uttara Kannada's Western Ghats. It is a natural landscape as well as a place with local religious traditions.
places.image_alt: Rock formations at Yana in Uttara Kannada
places.historical_background: Yana's geological formations and nearby sacred associations belong to different kinds of history. This entry does not assign an unsupported age or construction date.
places.cultural_significance: Local pilgrimage and nature-based visits meet at Yana; the site should be approached with respect for both its ecological setting and sacred use.
places.geographical_importance: The formations are set in the forested Western Ghats of Uttara Kannada.
